page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM-based instance driven by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors running under the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a 3.3 GHz clock frequency, eliminating hyperthreading overhead with a 1:1 core-to-thread allocation. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include dedicated hardware AES encryption acceleration, 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and an integrated 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume.

Benchmark results highlight strong per-core instruction efficiency and robust memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core performance (2393.0) and PassMark memory metrics (4380.5), complemented by top-tier single-threaded compression throughput in both gzip (36.48 GB/sec) and bzip3 (17.31 GB/sec). Multi-core throughput remains strong, logging a Geekbench multi-core score of 19899.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 257.74 GB/sec. Web serving and transactional operations perform solidly, yielding 54.77 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks, 29,397.82 in PassMark database operations, and 48.58 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Medium-sized LLM text generation (7B model) delivers a strong 29.71 tokens per second.

Because the instance pairs balanced compute and memory ratios with bundled high-speed local NVMe storage, it delivers notable operational efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads without relying solely on network-attached storage. The primary tradeoff lies in the arm64 architecture, requiring ARM-compatible application binaries, alongside the lack of x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX. The m9gd.4xlarge is well aligned for transactional databases, caching layers, data transformation pipelines, CI/CD compilation runners, and high-concurrency web application serving requiring low-latency scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 16-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Operating under the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory at a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an integrated 950 GB NVMe SSD local instance store and 8 Gbps baseline networking. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core Geekbench performance (2393.0), top-decile memory marks (4380.5), and strong multi-core execution (19899.0). Data compression tests demonstrate exceptional throughput, exceeding 36 GB/sec in gzip, while database operations reach strong percentiles. The absence of x86 vector extensions requires ARM-native workloads, but the bundled NVMe storage and dedicated physical core architecture provide strong resource density. It is suited for relational and key-value databases, caching nodes, continuous integration builds, and dynamic web applications needing high-speed local disk buffering.
